title.narrative: Ind OO1.3: Share of seats held by women in Moldovas parliament and local bodies. Local level: % of women elected as mayors at local level.

description.narrative: Ind OO1.3: Share of seats held by women in Moldovas parliament and local bodies. Local level: % of women elected as mayors at local level.% of women elected as mayors at local level

comment.narrative: The Project has set ambitious indicators concerning reaching a higher level of women participation in electoral process. Provided the relative political stability general Parliamentary elections will be held in 2025 the status of indicators are as followsWomen elected as MPs in national parliamentary elections compared to the baseline year 2020 the number of women elected as MPs increased by 1584 from 2425 to 40 59 Compared to the first year of Action implementation 2021 this number increased by 198 from 3861 in year to 40 59 in 2024 it should be mentioned that the increase here is due to certain MPs renouncing their mandate for other positions and the persons next on the list for the seat in Parliament were women. Currently from 101 MPs 41 are women. Women elected in local elections mayors indicator increase by 19 to 241 in 2023 as compared to 222 of elected mayors prior to electionsin the year 2020. Women elected in local elections council members in level 1 LPAs raions indicator increased by 43 to 403 as compared to 36 prior to elections in the year 2020.Women elected in local elections council members in level 2 LPAs villagescommunes indicator increased by 63 to 333 as compared to 27 prior to elections in the year 2020 prior to the local general elections. Although work remains to be done in order to reach the overall national objectives according to forecasts the 40 desired level of of women as mayors and in local elected bodies will be reached only by 2035 the general elections in 2023 showed a record number of women registered as well as being elected to office. Considering the 68 women trained by the Action who ran for public office with 47 being elected the Action had a significant contribution to the enhancement of the national indicators in gender equality.

comment.narrative: The purpose of the training was to provide a framework for effective public policy development from a gender perspective. The programme included the dynamic nature of the policy making process studying and discussing the factors influencing DMs and reaching a higher level of understanding on how different groups contribute to the policy making paradigm. The training also focused on the importance of influencing policies particularly for mainstreaming gender into different local decisions and plans. The practical part of the training involved identifying policy gaps in terms of responding to the needs of vulnerable groups specifically women form rural and remote areas. Prior to the Action the role of CSOs at local level in policy making was low but it has improved in the four target raions through the Gender Audit and Gender Action Plan by engaging the CSOs in the GAP development and monitoring processes.

comment.narrative: All four GAPs were approved for longer periods of time in line with the raion leadership political mandate and include now more activities related to the cooperation between local authorities and CSOs. The second interim report explained the process through which this indicator was achieved. Although the GAPs were approved in all four raions with Rezina integrating a series of actions in its development strategy as opposed to approving a separate decision on the GAP the local general elections caused some concern as to whether the GAPs will continue to be implemented by the new raion leadership. Keeping in mind the objective of promoting the scaling up of the GAs and GAPs experience gained in the four target raions the Action conducted advocacy monitoring visits to the raions to ensure that the GAPs will continue to be a priority for the raional councils. The advocacy visit proved highly successful. The newly elected officials showed openness not only in implementing the GAPs but also in updating them. It is important to mention that in some raions certain activities from the GAPs were already successfully implemented. For instance Telenesti has started to plan organize and carry out the very first Civil Society Fair at raion level in May 2024 where opportunities on how to better work together will be analysed. Also in Telenesti the internal regulation on the official days off for civil servants the collective labour agreement was amended from the gender equality perspective before only women were allowed to have the first and last days of school off while following the amendments to the Collective Labour Agreement at present this is relevant also for men to reflect specific family circumstances. This is a great example of not only mainstreaming gender in local policies but also of a better understanding of the actual needs of men and women and granting them equal rights in taking care of their children.

These activities provided a platform for dialogue and cooperation between DMs and CSOs and other relevant stakeholders with a view to enhancing the public policies from the gender equality perspective. The stakeholders included a wide range of public institutions the Parliament Government relevant ministries government implementing agencies civil society organisations academia and journalists. The advocacy activities to discuss policy recommendations translated in improved public policies at the national and local levels. They also led to important spill over effects. For instance a scientific researcher and speaker in the public discussion about women in science and research following the advocacy event of the project willing to contribute to improved state of affairs and womens situation in the research field applied for and obtained the position of Director of the National Research and Development Agency. This is just one example of the indirect impact of the advocacy activities.

comment.narrative: The initiatives focused on promoting womens rights raising awareness on gender equality developing local gender action plans economic empowerment of women. Given the limited capacities of the grassroots CSOs grant beneficiaries in project management the Action delivered capacity building trainings in project management financial management narrative and financial reporting communications and visibility in line with the requirements for the EU funded initiatives. The Action also delivered individual coaching to the grant beneficiaries during the project implementation.
